chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ammar ibn Marwan, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'My father was visited by death, so he was told to bequeath. He said, 'This is my son' — meaning Umar — 'so whatever he does, it is valid.' Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'Your father has bequeathed and has been concise.' I said, 'He ordered such and such for you.' He said, 'It is valid.' I said, 'And he bequeathed the emancipation of a believing, knowledgeable slave-girl. When we emancipated her, it became clear to us that she was not of sound judgment (minor).' He said, 'It is valid for him. The example of that is like a man who buys a sacrificial animal on the understanding that it is fat, but finds it thin. It is valid for him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a bequeathed slave-girl is found to be a minor upon emancipation?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the father's general bequest of his son's judgment, illustrating the Shia legal principle that a testator's intent is respected even if the specific object of the bequest has a latent defect. The analogy of the sacrificial animal (*udhiyah*) being thinner than expected underscores that minor imperfections do not invalidate the fulfillment of the religious or legal obligation, provided the core requirement is met. This reflects the broader Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the validity of actions based on the presumed soundness of the testator's knowledge unless proven otherwise.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ammar Bin Marwan who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Death presented itself to my father, so it was said to him, ‘Bequeath’. So he said, ‘This is my son’ – meaning Umar – ‘so whatever he does, so he is allowed to do so’. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Your father had bequeathed and it is allowed’. I said to him, ‘So he had ordered to you with such and such’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allowed’. I said, ‘And he bequeathed with (the emancipation) of the believing understanding slave-girl, so when I emancipated her it became clear to us that she had yet to come of age’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘It is allowed. But rather, the example of that is like the example of a man who buys a sacrificial animal upon the (understanding) that it is fat, so he finds it as thin. So it counts for him (allowed)’.
en.sarwar: 17. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Ammar ibn Marwan who has narrated the following: “

I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘My father was about to die and he was told to make a will.’ He said, ‘This is my son, meaning, ‘Umar. Whatever he does is permissible.’ Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said to him, ‘Your father has made a will and has made it concise.’ I said, ‘He has designated for you such and such amount.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘You can execute it.’ I then said that he made a will to free a believing well-informed slave but when we freed it was found out that the slave was born out of wedlock.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is sufficient. It is like one who buys an animal for sacrificial offering thinking that it is healthy, but finds it out to be skinnier but it is sufficient to meet the legal requirement.’”
